correctness.rationale: For the unit-edge star with μ>0 and 3≤k≤m+1, the leaf-block Schur complement is μ(μ+m+1)/(μ+1). The hub–leaf and distinct-leaf inverse entries are (μ+1)b and b, with b=[μ(μ+1)(μ+m+1)]⁻¹. The deterministic diagonal contributes the trace, and distinct unordered sign pairs are uncorrelated, giving variance 4 times the sum of within-class squared off-diagonal entries. After dividing by 4b² and fixing h hub-class leaves, a transfer from size u to v decreases the cost by u−v−1 when u≥v+2. Thus all and only balanced leaf-only assignments attain the fixed-h minimum. With r=k−1 and α=(μ+1)², the first difference is α+h−floor((m−h−1)/r), strictly increasing on its domain. It yields the full optimizer classification, including adjacent ties and the condition at h=0. For k=m+1 the only feasible occupancy is h=0 and the stated test has right-hand side zero. For m=9, k=3, μ=1/2, F(0)=16, F(1)=57/4 and F(2)=29/2, so the claimed 7/64 relative saving is exact.
residual_risks: The supplied 35,280 exact rational comparisons were inspected, not replayed. They test a finite set of shifts and sizes; the proof covers all stated parameters.

value.rationale: As mathematical content, the classification answers an actual probe-design question: at the same number of quadratic forms, the best coloring can be strictly worse than an improper partition. The exact threshold and all equality cases are useful for deciding when proper coloring loses in this model. The originality failure means this utility does not establish an additional distinct contribution by the submitted record.
residual_risks: No general-graph, correlated-probe or runtime conclusion is established.
